description: Names of the AutoSA modules the latency model maximizes over. This pack reads a generated design. It does not ask an agent to emit an AutoSA netlist.

skills.pattern: design latency is taken from the kernel top, or from a renamed mm_pe, instead of the generated module latencies
skills.strategy: predict_design_latency maximizes over the modules in latency_est. On mm1024 candidate 15 (space-time 0) those include PE, A_IO_L1_in, A_IO_L2_in, B_IO_L2, B_PE_dummy, and C_drain_IO_L1_out / C_drain_IO_L2_out. Space-time 3 adds L3 I/O. Space-time 4 and 5 use C_IO_L2_out rather than C_drain. Space-time 2 uses A_IO_L1, B_IO_L1, and C_IO.
required_steps: list the *_loop_info.json module names before quoting a latency
include PE and the longest I/O or drain module in the max
keep inter_trans and intra_trans under their outer module
guards: the GEMM-family pack forbids emitting these interconnect names; this skill only reads them

skills.pattern: every space-time is described as a local C buffer, or every space-time is described as a reduction across PEs
skills.strategy: Designs 1 and 4 (space-time 0 and 3) accumulate C inside the PE and drain it, so the generated graph has C_drain_IO. Design 5 (space-time 4) accumulates C along k, so the graph has C_IO_L2_out and no local bufC of that kind. Space-time 2 and 5 follow the reduction side.
required_steps: if the module list contains C_drain_IO, call C a drained local buffer
if the module list contains C_IO_L2_out and no C_drain_IO, call C a reduction across PEs
guards: do not expect array contraction on a C_drain design
